value.text: Uncontrolled seizure disorder — theophylline lowers the seizure threshold.

warnings.value: Narrow therapeutic index requiring level monitoring. Many interacting drugs (e.g. certain macrolides and fluoroquinolones) raise theophylline levels via CYP1A2/3A4 inhibition. Smoking induces its metabolism, so smokers typically need different handling than non-smokers.

foodLifestyle.value: Caffeine intake and smoking status both affect levels — keep both consistent and tell your pharmacist if either changes.

pregnancy.value: Pregnancy category / trimester notes pending sourced publish from authoritative SA-appropriate references.

overdoseSevereSigns.value: Arrhythmia or seizures in toxicity are a medical emergency.

antidoteOrSupportive.value: No specific antidote — toxicity is managed supportively with levels monitored under specialist care.

clinicalPearls.value: Theophylline's narrow therapeutic index plus its long interaction list (macrolides, fluoroquinolones, smoking status) is exactly why it has moved down the treatment ladder over time.

counsellingPoints.value: Report nausea, tremor or palpitations. Tell your pharmacist about your smoking status and any new antibiotics before starting them.

mechanism.value: Clarithromycin inhibits the CYP pathways that clear theophylline, raising levels toward toxicity in a drug with an already narrow therapeutic index.

action.value: Do not invent a dose change — flag for theophylline level monitoring and clinical review whenever both are co-prescribed.

lessons.title: Blue inhaler mental model
lessons.body: SABA relieves bronchospasm quickly. Over-reliance can mask uncontrolled asthma — educational framing for counter conversations.

lessons.title: Technique before more medicine
lessons.body: Poor MDI technique wastes medicine. Spacer counselling often helps more than inventing a new dose — Materia refuses to invent puff counts.

quiz.prompt: A patient uses their salbutamol inhaler many times daily and still wheezes. Best educational frame?
choices: Frequent reliever use can mean poor control — check technique and escalate to the clinician; do not invent a dose
quiz.teachFromMiss: Reliever overuse is a control signal — refer clinically; Materia never invents inhaler regimens.
